redis-cache is the only 'shared' datastore in pricing-engine's dependency graph and is consumed by four components: auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service all have `-> redis-cache kind: cache` edges. It is owner=platform, type=redis, shared=true.

Callers of pricing-engine: order-service -> pricing-engine (http), and api-gateway -> order-service -> pricing-engine; api-gateway also reaches market-data-service and portfolio-service directly. So pricing latency propagates to order-service and the trading screens behind api-gateway.

The single shared component on that path is redis-cache (platform-owned, shared=true), used by pricing-engine AND market-data-service — and also by auth-service and portfolio-service. events.statement: pricing-engine p99 latency was flat at ~59-62ms (max ~66ms) from 09:00 through the 13:08 bucket, then jumped in the 13:16 bucket to avg 601.68ms / max 2227.82ms, and stayed elevated (13:24 avg 2211.36ms, max 2309.91ms). Onset (p99 > 2s) is therefore between 13:08 and 13:16 UTC.

First ERROR log in pricing-engine is 2026-04-09T13:23:57Z: 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took 5171ms'. The dominant error signature is 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' with count 192 out of 197 matched logs — a downstream-timeout signature naming market-data-service, with observed durations 827ms to 8456ms. No 5xx/connection-refused pattern appears in the top patterns.

pricing-engine error_rate (HTTP 5xx %) was ~0.17-0.24% through the 13:12 bucket, then rose in the 13:21 bucket to avg 3.32% / max 4.37% and held ~4% (e.g. 13:30 avg 4.11%, 14:51 avg 4.02%). The 5xx elevation begins in the same 13:21 bucket as the latency jump.

pricing-engine's own resource metrics are flat across the onset: cpu_pct stays ~39-40% (max 44.48, min 34.59) and memory_pct stays ~48-49% (max 54.93, min 43.36) from 12:00 through 14:51, with no step change at 13:16-13:21. This indicates no CPU or memory saturation in pricing-engine itself.

market-data-service p99 latency is flat at ~39-40ms through the 13:12 bucket, then jumps in the SAME 13:21 bucket to avg 1702.29ms / max 1979.98ms (13:30 avg 1814.5ms). This matches the pricing-engine subnet of errors naming market-data-service as the slow downstream and places market-data-service's own latency onset in the 13:12-13:21 window.

The reported degradation is consistent with a downstream (market-data-service) slowdown rather than pricing-engine saturation: pricing-engine CPU/memory are flat while its p99 and 5xx rise and 192/197 of its warn/error logs attribute the exceeded deadline to market-data-service taking up to 8456ms. Trading-screen impact propagates pricing-engine -> market-data-service is the shared upstream.

tasks.answer: pricing-engine's quote-serving path is pricing-engine → market-data-service → exchange-gateway → exchange-api (external), with pricing-engine also reading redis-cache directly. The single shared component on that path is redis-cache (platform-owned, shared=true), used by pricing-engine AND market-data-service — and also by auth-service and portfolio-service. That makes redis-cache the most likely shared bottleneck candidate, with market-data-service and the external exchange-api as the other upstream single points on the quote path.
